subject: Applied Thermodynamics
summary: the air-standard Otto, Diesel and dual cycles (efficiency, mean effective pressure, cut-off and pressure ratios, comparisons) and IC engine performance: indicated and brake power, mechanical, thermal, volumetric and relative efficiencies, bsfc, the Morse test and the heat balance

questions.text: The air-standard efficiency of the Otto cycle depends on
opts: the compression ratio and γ only
questions.ans: (B) the compression ratio and γ only
solution: Concept: ηOtto = 1 − 1/rγ−1.
Only the compression ratio r and the ratio of specific heats γ appear: (B).
The heat supplied changes the work and the MEP, not the air-standard efficiency.
Exam tip: Real SI engines cannot raise r beyond about 10–12 because of knock, which caps their efficiency.

questions.text: An air-standard Otto cycle (γ = 1.4) has an efficiency of 55 %. Its compression ratio (round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Invert η = 1 − 1/rγ−1.
Exam tip: Each step up in r gives a smaller gain in η: going from r = 7.36 to 10 adds only about 5 percentage points.

questions.text: In an air-standard Diesel cycle 1–2–3–4 (1–2 isentropic compression, 2–3 constant-pressure heat addition), the cut-off ratio is defined as
solution: Concept: Cut-off ratio ρ is the volume ratio over which fuel is burnt (heat is added) at constant pressure.
ρ = V3/V2 (C). V1/V2 is the compression ratio r.
The expansion ratio is V<sub>4</sub>/V<sub>3</sub> = r/ρ.
Exam tip: Cut-off as a percentage of stroke = (ρ − 1)/(r − 1) × 100.

questions.text: An air-standard Diesel cycle (γ = 1.4) has a compression ratio of 16 and a cut-off ratio of 2.5. Its thermal efficiency (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: ηDiesel = 1 − (1/rγ−1)(ργ − 1)/[γ(ρ − 1)].
Exam tip: The Otto cycle with r = 16 would give 67.0 %: the bracket term is the Diesel penalty.

questions.text: Although the Otto cycle is more efficient than the Diesel cycle for the same compression ratio, practical CI (diesel) engines are more efficient than SI engines mainly because
opts: diesel fuel has a much higher calorific value
CI engines run at higher speeds
CI engines work at much higher compression ratios (about 15–22), as only air is compressed
questions.ans: (D) CI engines work at much higher compression ratios (about 15–22), as only air is compressed
solution: Concept: In a CI engine only air is compressed and fuel is injected at the end, so there is no knock limit on compression.
Compression ratios of 15–22 against 8–12 for SI engines more than make up for the Diesel cycle penalty: (D).
CI engines also run lean and unthrottled, reducing pumping losses at part load.
Exam tip: Compare cycles at equal maximum pressure to see why: the Diesel cycle then wins.

questions.text: An engine has an indicated power of 60 kW and a mechanical efficiency of 80 %. It burns 15 kg/h of fuel of calorific value 42 000 kJ/kg. Its brake thermal efficiency (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: ηbth = bp/(ṁf × CV), with bp = ηm × ip.
Fuel energy = 15 × 42 000/3600 = 175 kW
ηbth = 48/175 = 27.43 % (indicated thermal efficiency = 60/175 = 34.29 %)
Exam tip: ηbth = ηm × ηith.

questions.text: In a rope brake dynamometer, W is the dead load, S the spring balance reading, D the effective brake-drum diameter (m) and N the speed (rpm). The brake power (kW) is
solution: Concept: Brake torque T = (W − S) × D/2 (net rope tension × drum radius).
bp = 2πNT/60 = 2πN(W − S)(D/2)/60 W = (W − S)πDN/60 W
In kW: (W − S)πDN/60 000 (A), with D = drum + rope diameter.
Exam tip: All the brake power is dissipated as heat in the drum, which must be water-cooled.

questions.text: A four-cylinder four-stroke engine (bore 90 mm, stroke 100 mm) develops a brake power of 40 kW at 3000 rpm. Its brake mean effective pressure (in bar, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: bp = pmb × Vs × (N/2)/60 × number of cylinders for a four-stroke engine.
V<sub>s</sub> = (π/4)(0.09)² × 0.1 = 6.362 × 10<sup>−4</sup> m³ per cylinder
Swept volume rate = 4 × 6.362 × 10<sup>−4</sup> × 1500/60 = 0.06362 m³/s
Exam tip: Do not forget N/2 for four-stroke engines; a two-stroke engine uses N.

questions.text: The p–V diagram shown is that of an air-standard dual (limited-pressure) cycle. In this cycle heat is added
opts: during 2–3 at constant volume and during 3–4 at constant pressure
during 2–3 at constant pressure and during 3–4 at constant volume
questions.ans: (A) during 2–3 at constant volume and during 3–4 at constant pressure
solution: Concept: The dual cycle burns part of the fuel at constant volume (near TDC) and the rest at constant pressure.
2–3: vertical line, constant-volume heat addition; 3–4: horizontal line, constant-pressure heat addition: (A).
4–5 is isentropic expansion and 5–1 constant-volume heat rejection.
Exam tip: With pressure ratio α = 1 it becomes the Diesel cycle; with cut-off ratio ρ = 1 it becomes the Otto cycle.

questions.text: An air-standard dual cycle (γ = 1.4) has a compression ratio of 15, a pressure ratio of 1.4 during constant-volume heating and a cut-off ratio of 1.5. Its thermal efficiency (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: η = 1 − (1/rγ−1)(αργ − 1)/[(α − 1) + γα(ρ − 1)].
Exam tip: Check against limits: Otto (r = 15) gives 66.15 %, so the dual value must be lower.

questions.text: Beyond a certain speed, the volumetric efficiency of an engine falls as the speed increases, mainly because
opts: the flow losses (friction and choking) across the intake valve rise sharply with the gas velocity
questions.ans: (B) the flow losses (friction and choking) across the intake valve rise sharply with the gas velocity
solution: Concept: Volumetric efficiency = actual air inducted/(swept volume × ambient density).
At high speed the gas velocity through the valve rises, the pressure drop grows roughly with velocity squared and the flow can choke: (B).
At low speed, back-flow through the late-closing intake valve lowers it instead, so η<sub>v</sub> peaks at a mid speed.
Exam tip: Valve timing (inlet closing after BDC) uses the inertia of the charge to raise ηv.

questions.text: An air-standard Otto cycle has a compression ratio of 8. At the start of compression the air is at 100 kPa and 300 K, and 1500 kJ/kg of heat is added (c<sub>v</sub> = 0.718 kJ/kg·K, γ = 1.4). The maximum pressure in the cycle (in MPa, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Isentropic compression, then constant-volume heat addition; use p3v3/T3 = p1v1/T1 with v3 = v1/r.
Exam tip: p2 = 100 × 81.4 = 1838 kPa; heat addition multiplies it by T3/T2 = 4.03.

questions.text: The relative efficiency of an IC engine is defined as
solution: Concept: Relative (efficiency) ratio compares the real engine with its ideal air-standard cycle at the same compression ratio.
ηrel = ηactual/ηair-standard: (C). Typical values are 0.6–0.8.
Option (A) is the mechanical efficiency.
Exam tip: If ηith = 30 % and the Otto value is 56.5 %, ηrel = 0.53.

questions.text: An air-standard Diesel cycle has a compression ratio of 18, with air at 300 K at the start of compression. 1200 kJ/kg of heat is added at constant pressure (c<sub>p</sub> = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, γ = 1.4). The cut-off ratio (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: In constant-pressure heat addition, ρ = V3/V2 = T3/T2.
Exam tip: More heat (higher load) means a larger cut-off ratio and a lower Diesel-cycle efficiency.

questions.text: The compression ratio of a petrol (SI) engine is limited mainly by
opts: the strength of the connecting rod
solution: Concept: In an SI engine the fuel–air mixture is compressed together.
At high compression ratios the end gas self-ignites before the flame reaches it, causing knock (D).
Higher-octane fuel, a compact chamber and cooler intake allow higher r.
Exam tip: In CI engines the opposite holds: a higher compression ratio reduces diesel knock by shortening the ignition delay.
